record.title: NIST’s new adversarial-ML draft adds a taxonomy for agentic-system attacks
record.summary: NIST’s 9 November initial public draft SP 2400-102e2026 extends its adversarial machine-learning taxonomy to agentic systems. Section 4 classifies attacks across workflow stages and attacker capabilities, including attacks using untrusted data and memory, malicious tools and skills, compromised agents in multi-agent systems, and long-horizon task persistence. NIST says the taxonomy is intended to inform future standards and practice guides; public comments are open through 18 December. This is a voluntary draft, not evidence of adoption or of defense effectiveness.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: NIST published SP 2400-102e2026 as an initial public draft on 9 November 2026, with comments due 18 December.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The draft includes a dedicated agentic-systems taxonomy covering attacks across workflow stages, untrusted data, malicious tools and skills, multi-agent systems, and long-horizon tasks.

claims.label: INFERRED
claims.text: Relative to NIST AI 100-2 E2025’s predictive and generative system coverage, the draft’s separate agentic taxonomy is a scope expansion for NIST’s AML reference.

evidence_gaps.description: The report is open for comment; the final taxonomy, adoption by standards groups, and use in evaluation practice remain unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If used by standards groups and evaluators, an agent-specific attack taxonomy can change security review and evaluation coverage; its consequence is meaningful but bounded because this is a voluntary draft with no demonstrated adoption or effect.
limitations: This is an initial public draft and voluntary reference, not a binding rule or evidence of adoption.
The taxonomy’s completeness and practical usefulness have not been independently evaluated in this activation.
The report does not demonstrate that listed mitigations prevent agent attacks or reduce incidents.

technical.claimed_result: NIST presents an agentic-systems attack taxonomy and describes it as a basis for future standards and practice guides.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official draft and publication record establish the document’s status, stated scope, taxonomy headings and comment period. They do not demonstrate adoption, completeness, mitigation efficacy or reduced security incidents.
technical.mechanism: A conceptual classification organizes attacks by agent-workflow stage and attacker capability/objective, with dedicated sections on untrusted data, tools and skills, multi-agent systems and long-horizon operation.
technical.regime: NIST SP 2400-102e2026 initial public draft, with focus on agentic AI systems; voluntary and open to public comment through 18 December 2026.
technical.reproducibility: Publication status and text are directly inspectable in NIST’s official record and PDF. No empirical evaluation or implementation outcome is claimed.
technical.strongest_baseline: NIST AI 100-2 E2025, which classified predictive and generative AI adversarial-ML risks but did not have this dedicated agentic-system taxonomy.

brief.title: NIST’s new adversarial-ML draft adds a taxonomy for agentic-system attacks
brief.why_it_matters: NIST’s 2025 taxonomy covered predictive and generative systems; this draft explicitly treats agents’ tools, memory, peers and persistent state as security surfaces. That gives evaluators and standards groups an official, agent-specific vocabulary while the field works through how to assess these risks. The draft remains open for comment and does not establish that the proposed taxonomy or mitigations are adopted or effective.
